A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same EDF method and Comp-DD benchmark. Their main text, appendices, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original EDF experiments on ImageNet subsets and Comp-DD, together with component ablations, cross-architecture evaluation, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds simple-dataset comparisons, Grad-CAM model sensitivity results, and activation-extraction latency measurements.

M1.justification: Equations 1–5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same parameterwise low-loss filtering, Grad-CAM gradient weighting, and periodic activation-map updates. Both appendices still describe DATM/PAD-based distillation of images and soft labels.

E1.justification: v2 adds Tiny-ImageNet evaluation in Table 3, modestly extending classification coverage. Its new EDF comparisons on CIFAR-10 concern a dataset already used in v1 Figure 1. The ImageNet subsets and evaluated Comp-DD categories remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v1 Table 2 compares EDF with random selection and full-data training; v2 adds DATM at IPC200 and IPC300 on ImageMeow and ImageYellow. Comparator membership in the retained ImageNet, Comp-DD, cross-architecture, and no-KD comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: The documented ImageWoof IPC10 enhancement factor changes from 2 in v1 Table 8 to 1 in v2 Table 9, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Added protocols include CIFAR-10 IPC500, four Grad-CAM backbones at IPC1/10/50, and extraction timing at IPC1/10/50/200/300.

E4.justification: Appendices 11.5–11.6 add targeted analyses of sensitivity to the Grad-CAM backbone and activation-extraction overhead. Existing component, dropout, threshold, update-frequency, cross-architecture, distortion, and activation-trend analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing ± reporting practice is retained and extended to new benchmark rows. Neither PDF specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v2 introduces no confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Substantial new result entries cover high-IPC DATM comparisons, CIFAR-10/Tiny-ImageNet, Grad-CAM model variants, and latency. For example, Table 3 reports Tiny-ImageNet IPC1 EDF at 17.8±0.2 versus DATM at 17.1±0.3 under DD, but EDF at 10.3±0.4 versus RDED at 12.0±0.1 with KD. Existing matched accuracy values are retained.

T1.justification: The loss, filtering rule, gradient weighting, and complexity metric retain the same mathematics. Writing the complexity threshold as a variable explicitly set to 0.5 and changing multiplication notation are equivalent restatements. No proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of improving complex-scenario distillation through CPD/DAE, achieving the first lossless performance on some ImageNet subsets, and introducing sixteen easy/hard Comp-DD subsets. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion preserve these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning generalization to simple datasets, limited sensitivity to the trained Grad-CAM backbone, negligible extraction overhead, and applicability to other matching methods. It removes v1's explicit limitations paragraph about computational cost and exclusive reliance on Grad-CAM; the complexity-metric bias caveat remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies ResNet18 as the Grad-CAM extractor, reports timing information, and describes code and benchmark access as publicly released. However, it removes the label-learning-rate columns from v1 Tables 8 and 11, now Tables 9 and 14, while retaining soft-label distillation.

R1.justification: Cited coverage expands substantially into theoretical, robustness, multimodal, and newer distillation research, although many additions appear only in a citation list. Section 6 adds DD-Ranking and fairness-oriented benchmark positioning; the appendix survey adds NCFD, MIM4DD, DQAS, and LDD. The earlier applications paragraph and its citations are removed.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order are retained, with localized shortening and clarification of trajectory-matching terminology. Appendices A–F become supplementary Sections 9–14, acknowledgements become Section 8, and citations change from author-year to numeric form.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column presentation, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables. Three results tables are added, the component ablation panels are merged, and hyperparameter table columns are removed. Figure 5's reversed subfigure descriptions are corrected.

improvement.justification: Adding DATM to the high-IPC comparison and providing simple-dataset, Grad-CAM sensitivity, and timing results modestly strengthen the paper's evidence. These benefits are partly offset by removed label-learning-rate details and deletion of the explicit limitations discussion. The core method and principal results remain stable.
